To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the apparent permeability of the human kidney is substantially affected by movement of fluid and tracer between the renal cortex and medullary regions.
Patlak analysis can be performed on dynamic CT data, that permeability is greater in the medulla than in the cortex in most cases, and that permeability correlates well with plasma urea.

Patlak analysis applied to CT data is useful in the measurement of renal filtration function, and the apparent variations in permeability between renal cortex and medullary reflect movement of fluid and intrarenal contrast medium.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of dynamic CT for measuring renal function.
the development of new techniques for the measurement of renal function and perfusion by dynamic CT and with the development of methods for the analysis of the resulting data.
the development of new methods for the quantitative analysis of CT data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Patlak images do reflect renal function and are diagnostically useful, but that the images are not a true representation of intrarenal permeabilities.
Patlak analysis of CT data is not suitable for the assessment of renal function.
Patlak images are not useful for the measurement of permeability, but they may be useful diagnostically for the measurement of renal function.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Patlak images are a useful tool in the investigation of renal function but that their interpretation must be made with caution.
CT derived Patlak images do provide information about kidney function but the images are substantially affected and distorted by the fluid movement between renal segments.
Patlak CT is useful for measuring whole kidney filtration function but not intrarenal permeabilities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Patlak analysis of dynamic CT images can provide information about the concentrating function of the kidney.

CT measurements of whole renal perfusion are useful for assessing renal function but the apparent variations in intrarenal perfusion are artefactual and should not be used to assess the concentrating ability of individual kidneys.
Patlak images do NOT reflect true intrarenally permeability values.
